duties:
The TAs will support an interdisciplinary graduate course examining the relationship between artificial intelligence and cities. The course combines critical inquiry with collaborative design thinking and project-based learning.
TAs will support students in developing projects from problem framing and critical analysis through concept development, prototyping, critique, and iteration. They will assist students in identifying appropriate methods and tools for translating critical ideas about AI and urban issues into feasible design interventions, which may include interactive websites, mobile application concepts, data visualizations, maps, games, conversational systems, community toolkits, digital publications, or physical/digital prototypes.
Duties may include facilitating classroom discussions and design activities; supporting individual students and project teams during studio/workshop sessions; providing technical and conceptual guidance on prototyping; offering feedback on project development and presentations; assisting with course administration and assessment; and meeting with the instructor as required.
The ideal TAs will be comfortable moving between critical discussion and making, and will be able to support students with varying levels of technical and design experience.

Physical computing: Arduino, micro, sensors, or related platforms

Experience facilitating interdisciplinary teamwork and providing constructive design critique.

qualifications_minimum:
Applicants must demonstrate all of the following: 

Academic qualifications 

    A Bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline, and current enrollment in (or completion of) a graduate-level program (Master's or Doctoral) in a health-related discipline. 

    A research area or field of study closely related to the course material, with formal graduate-level coursework in research methods, epidemiology, biostatistics, or an equivalent methods-focused area. 

Subject-matter knowledge 
 Demonstrated command of the core content of the course, sufficient to teach it at the second-year undergraduate level, including: 

    the nature of scientific inquiry and the role of empirical evidence in health research; 

    formulating research questions and hypotheses, and locating and appraising published literature; 

    epidemiological and other study designs (e.g., randomized trials, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and non-experimental/observational designs; surveys; literature reviews); 

    quantitative and qualitative approaches to health research; 

    measurement, sampling, validity, reliability, bias, and confounding; 

    ethical conduct of research involving human participants. 

Teaching and course design 

    Demonstrated ability to design a syllabus in accordance with department guidelines, including a coherent assessment plan and alignment of assessments to stated learning outcomes. 

    Demonstrated ability to lecture to a large class and to coordinate content across multiple tutorial sections. 

    Demonstrated ability to explain research design and methodological concepts to a second-year undergraduate audience with varied levels of prior quantitative preparation. 

    Demonstrated ability to develop, administer, and mark assignments, tests, and examinations, and to prepare rubrics and answer keys in advance of grading. 

Supervision and coordination 

    Demonstrated ability to supervise and coordinate a teaching assistant team, including assigning work, norming grading standards, and ensuring consistency and accuracy of marks across sections. 

Technical proficiency 

    Quercus or an equivalent learning management system. 

    Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). 

Other requirements 

    Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. 

    Professional standard of conduct befitting an academic environment, including punctuality and reliable attendance. 

    Ability to manage a high-volume academic workload and meet strict institutional deadlines (e.g., grade submission, deferred assessments). 

    Ability to uphold academic integrity, student privacy, and confidentiality.
qualifications_preferred:
Preference may be given to applicants who demonstrate one or more of the following: 

Academic qualifications 

    Enrollment in a doctoral program (e.g., PhD, MD) or a completed doctoral degree, with a specialization directly relevant to the course. 

    An active research program in epidemiology, public health, health services research, global health, or a comparably methods-intensive field. 

    Peer-reviewed publications employing the study designs and methods taught in this course. 

Teaching experience 

    Prior experience as sole instructor of record for an undergraduate research methods, epidemiology, or statistics course. 

    Substantial teaching assistant experience in this course or a closely comparable course, with evidence of effective teaching of the relevant material. 

    Documented teaching effectiveness  

Demonstrated strengths in large-class pedagogy 

    Experience with at least one active-learning approach suited to a large enrolment course  

    Experience providing detailed feedback on study and research design. 

    Experience designing assessments that are resilient to generative AI use and that support academic integrity at scale. 

    Experience coordinating a large teaching team across multiple tutorial sections.

application_procedure: Applicants should submit a cover letter, CV, and the names and contact information of at least two references as a single PDF to academicskills.utm@utoronto.ca by Friday, August 21, 2026. Please use the subject line: “Math and Numeracy TA Application.”
duties:
This new Math and Numeracy program is an in-person academic support initiative designed to help students strengthen foundational mathematics knowledge and develop effective learning strategies. The program is designed to support students who are seeking to address knowledge gaps, reflect on their learning, build confidence, and prepare for first year university calculus courses. Through interactive instruction, facilitated group work, independent exercises, and feedback, the program aims to improve student readiness, retention, and overall academic success. The program is designed to primarily support students who intend to take first-year calculus classes (MAT 132/34, 135/36).

Working collaboratively with the Learning Strategist (Math & Numeracy Focus) and the Math and Numeracy Instructor, the TA will support this new Math and Numeracy program, a 4-week in-person program which combines a review of essential mathematical concepts (e.g., algebra, trigonometry, functions) with learning strategy instruction (e.g., critical thinking, problem solving, resilience, managing test anxiety). The TA will support curriculum development, attend lessons, facilitate group work during classes, lead drop-in and review sessions, mark assessments, and provides individualized student support and feedback. The TA will foster an inclusive and supportive learning environment that promotes student engagement and community-building.
